summary: A rare live-in, 12x12 cab on a 100-ft Aermotor tower built in 1937 in Alabama's Conecuh National Forest, one of only two of its kind left in the state.

facts.design: Live-in 12'x12' hip-roof wooden cab with catwalk on a 100-ft Aermotor steel tower

events.note: Registered June 9, 2015 as US 1076, AL 60, nominated by Al Pelham

evidence.supports: location in Conecuh National Forest, Escambia County, near Florida line
evidence.quote: Located in the Conecuh National Forest on the Florida state line, Parker Springs Lookout is an unusual live-in 12'x'12' hip roof cab with catwalk mounted on a 100' Aermotor tower.

Location
Conecuh National Forest
Escambia County, Alabama
It is a National Forest Service Tower and it Located in the Conecuh National Forest in Escambia County Al.

evidence.supports: unique design, only four left, two in Alabama
evidence.quote: Unique to the southern National Forests, there are only four left, two of them in Alabama. One of them is Open Pond Lookout nearby.

evidence.supports: Open Pond a few miles away, same forest
evidence.quote: Only two of these towers are still standing in Alabama the other is Open Pond which is a few miles away in the Conecuh National Forest also.
Parker Springs Lookout was built in 1937.

evidence.supports: only two wooden 12x12 towers with catwalks in Alabama, side entrances
evidence.quote: This tower and the Parker Springs Lookout which is also in the Conecuh National Forest are the only two wooden 12′ X 12′ towers with catwalks in the state of Alabama.

evidence.supports: side/bottom entrance layout rarity in far south Alabama
evidence.quote: It is one of three towers in the very Southern part of Alabama that have larger cabs and side entrances rather than the bottom entrances that the vast majority of those scattered through out the state have.

evidence.supports: nominated by Al Pelham, registered June 9 2015, US 1076 AL 60

notes_for_editor: No source found on staffing history, decommission date, restoration, or current public access/climbability for Parker Springs specifically. The built year (1937) comes from a single hobbyist survey site (Jackson's Ramblings), not an NRHP nomination or Forest Service document; treat it as plausible but not strongly corroborated. height_m (30.5) is a conversion of the 100-ft tower height stated by NHLR, not independently confirmed.
